title: New in the 2026 Exam Guide
description: What AWS added to the exam guide in April 2026, plus topics the other decks never taught. You learn each card here; the deck its topic belongs to lists it too, with your progress.

cards.definition: Agentic platform to build, deploy, and operate AI agents securely at scale with any framework or model, using modular services such as Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, and Policy.
Identity and credential management service for AI agents that lets them securely access AWS resources and third-party services on behalf of users, working with existing identity providers.
Deterministic rules, written in Cedar or natural language, that AgentCore Gateway checks before each agent tool call to control which tools and actions an agent may use.
AWS agentic AI-powered IDE that uses spec-driven development: it turns a request into requirements, a design, and a task list, then carries out the tasks to move from prototype to production.
Open-source SDK, first released by AWS, for building autonomous AI agents with a model-first approach; supports many FMs, MCP, and multi-agent patterns like Swarm, Graph, and Workflow.
AI-powered service where you chat with AI agents to automate tasks, analyze data (Quick Sight), build apps, and research; Amazon Q Business now directs new customers to it.
AWS service that uses agentic AI to speed up migration and modernization of workloads such as mainframe, VMware, and .NET, handing discovery, planning, and execution tasks to AI agents.
Amazon's own family of foundation models, accessed through Amazon Bedrock, for text and multimodal understanding, image and video generation, and speech.
Autonomous AI that acts independently to reach pre-set goals, proactively doing complex tasks without constant human oversight or step-by-step prompting.
Open-source standard for connecting AI applications and agents to external systems such as data sources, tools, and workflows; often described as a USB-C port for AI.
Designing systems that dynamically assemble the best set of information (instructions, memory, tool definitions, retrieved knowledge) in the context window for an LLM to do a task.
Amazon Bedrock Agents (now Agents Classic) pattern where a supervisor agent plans, splits a task, and routes parts to specialist collaborator agents that work in parallel.
Agent capability that keeps turn-by-turn context within one session and also extracts user preferences, facts, and summaries that persist across sessions.
You give a model tool definitions; the model decides when a tool is needed and requests it, then your app (or Amazon Bedrock) runs the tool and returns the result to the model.
Amazon Bedrock feature to build end-to-end generative AI workflows by linking prompts, FMs, knowledge bases, and AWS services like Lambda in a visual builder.
Amazon Bedrock feature to create, test, save, and reuse prompts with variables, compare prompt variants, and save prompt versions to deploy into applications.
Customization that transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller, faster, cheaper student model by fine-tuning the student on the teacher's responses.
Optional Amazon Bedrock feature that caches long, repeated prompt prefixes (like a shared document) so later requests skip reprocessing them, cutting latency and input token costs.
On-demand Amazon Bedrock inference is billed per token, with separate rates for input tokens and output tokens; in AWS's example, output tokens cost more.
Evaluation method where an evaluator LLM scores another (generator) model's responses on metrics like correctness, completeness, and harmfulness, and explains each score.
Automatic metric that compares generated text with a reference using BERT contextual embeddings and cosine similarity; Amazon Bedrock uses it to score summarization accuracy.
Ready-made prompt datasets used to evaluate models; Amazon Bedrock automatic evaluation offers built-in ones based on open-source sets like BOLD, TREX, and Gigaword, or you bring your own.
Providing a few example input-output pairs in the prompt so an LLM calibrates its output to your expectations; AWS uses it as another name for few-shot prompting.
Image-generation input in Amazon Nova Canvas listing objects or style traits to exclude from the output, such as "waves, clouds".
GenAI drawback where the same prompt can produce different outputs, so model outputs must be logged and inspected to validate correctness over time.
Measures of a GenAI application's business impact, such as ROI, efficiency, conversion rate, average revenue per user, and customer lifetime value.

cards.term: Agent metrics (task completion rate and cost per interaction)
cards.definition: Agent KPIs with measurable targets across latency, throughput, quality (share of tasks finished successfully), and efficiency (tokens per task, cost per completion).
SageMaker AI option for low-latency or high-throughput online predictions from a persistent, fully managed endpoint that handles sustained traffic (payloads up to 25 MB).
SageMaker AI option that queues requests with large payloads (up to 1 GB) and long processing times (up to 1 hour), and can scale the endpoint to zero when idle.
SageMaker AI option for intermittent or unpredictable traffic: AWS manages and scales the compute, you pay only for use, and idle endpoints can have cold starts.
Vulnerability management service that continually scans EC2 instances, ECR container images, and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.
Creates a private connection (interface VPC endpoint) between your VPC and Amazon Bedrock, so traffic needs no internet gateway, NAT device, or public IP addresses.
Stores, retrieves, and rotates secrets such as database credentials and API keys, so applications fetch them at runtime instead of hard-coding them.
Lets you launch AWS resources in a logically isolated virtual network that you define, with subnets, route tables, gateways, and endpoints controlling connectivity.

cards.term: Encryption at rest and in transit
cards.definition: Protecting stored data (for example with AWS KMS keys) and data moving over the network (TLS). Amazon Bedrock uses encryption to protect both.
Service where Bedrock publishes AWS/Bedrock metrics such as Invocations, InvocationLatency, InputTokenCount, and OutputTokenCount to monitor volume, latency, and tokens.
Bedrock setting, off by default, that records request data, response data, and metadata for model invocations and delivers them to CloudWatch Logs and/or Amazon S3.
AWS framework that sorts GenAI use cases into five scopes (Consumer app, Enterprise app, Pre-trained, Fine-tuned, and Self-trained models) to guide security controls.
Central repository of metadata (location, schema, runtime metrics) about your data sets. Crawlers populate it, and it helps users discover data and track lineage.
The requirement to keep data in a certain region or country to comply with local laws and regulations. It is one key aspect of data sovereignty.
Rules that automatically move S3 objects to lower-cost storage classes or expire (delete) them, for example after a regulatory compliance retention period.
Amazon S3 storage classes purpose-built for secure, durable, long-term data archiving at the lowest cost, for data you need to retain but rarely access.
Privacy-preserving ML techniques such as differential privacy, federated learning, and secure multi-party computation that train models while minimizing sensitive-data exposure.
Prompt attack that tries to extract the system prompt, developer instructions, or confidential configuration; Bedrock Guardrails detects it on the Standard tier only.
Prompt-attack aim of taking over the model's task, for example via persona takeover instructions; Bedrock Guardrails classifies these under prompt injection.
Exploit during model training or customization in which data not meant for training is used, causing undesirable model behavior that is hard to detect and remediate.
Legal risk that GenAI output infringes others' IP. AWS offers an uncapped IP indemnity for copyright claims on output of specified Amazon GenAI services that are used responsibly.
Bedrock Guardrails check that scores responses against a reference source and the user query, blocking those below your threshold as hallucinations.
Bedrock Guardrails feature that uses formal logic to validate model responses against policy rules you define, detecting factually incorrect statements and explaining why.
ML Lens pillar focused on environmental impact, especially energy consumption and efficiency, to reduce resource usage across the ML lifecycle.
Measuring disparity within subgroups (e.g., by department), as SageMaker Clarify's CDD metric does, to rule out Simpson's paradox hiding or reversing bias.
Foundation models come under licenses set by their source (for example Apache 2.0). You must review and comply with the license, and some models require accepting a EULA.
Search service whose k-NN search finds nearest-neighbor vectors by Euclidean distance or cosine similarity; OpenSearch Serverless and managed clusters can be a Bedrock knowledge base's vector store.
PostgreSQL extension (v0.5.0+, HNSW indexing) enabled on Aurora PostgreSQL so it can store vector embeddings as a Bedrock Knowledge Base vector store.
Bedrock Knowledge Bases feature that uses Amazon Neptune Analytics graphs to combine vector search with entity relationships, connecting facts across documents for RAG.
Tracks AWS costs and usage against budgets you set and alerts you by email or SNS when actual or forecasted amounts exceed a threshold. It can also trigger actions.
Tool to view and analyze AWS costs and usage, with up to 13 months of history and an 18-month spending forecast, to find cost trends and drivers.
